site.name: LINTHESIS
site.intro: I'm Mi Lin (Liam). Writing books and guides is how I think problems through; building software and atlases is how I give ideas form; open-sourcing and experimenting is how I share them.
site.author: Mi Lin / Liam

projects.title: DISCOVERY-TAXONOMY
projects.one_liner: Find a direction worth exploring: compare old assumptions with new shifts, then start with a fillable AI seed prompt.
projects.intro: A bilingual collection of exploration cards across building, business, content, cognition, career and life. Each card contrasts an old assumption with a new shift and includes real-world signals and seed prompts. Fill in your own context, copy a question and explore a direction you had not considered.
features: Six exploration arenas and five lenses, including cost collapse, role inversion and invisible friction
Compare assumptions and shifts, with linked signals and searchable tags
Fill prompt variables, copy a question or open it in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Perplexity
Random discovery, Chinese/English switching and shareable filter or card links
related: Inspect what AI actually delivers through concrete tasks, outputs and acceptance records.
After choosing a direction, find a fillable, reusable prompt for the task.

projects.title: Wenjian · AI Task Gallery
projects.intro: The main collection is organized around artifact-making tasks. Each task explains the required file, how to open it and how to assess completion. Recorded runs distinguish success, failure and partial verification and include inspectable outputs. Short questions remain as a warm-up collection.
features: Browse and search by output: animation, 3D scene, game, app and more
Full task prompts, file formats, opening instructions and acceptance criteria
Run records link to actual outputs and state execution conditions and verification status
Referenced and original tasks identify their sources; short questions have their own collection
projects.one_liner: Tasks that ask AI to make animations, 3D scenes, games and apps, with prompts, artifacts, run conditions and acceptance records.
projects.note: Displayed runs include Cursor assistance and tool use. They are not a ranking from blind tests of bare model APIs.

projects.title: Prompt Taxonomy
projects.sub: Find a prompt for the task
projects.intro: A bilingual prompt directory for research, writing, learning, data, development, product work and everyday tasks. Templates have fillable variables, workflows explain how steps connect, and research and public-case references can be traced to their sources.
features: 224 Chinese templates with a matching English catalog across 16 task categories
19 workflows that connect the output of one step to the next
Fill template variables, copy the result and share a link to the template
Search by task and evidence type; download the machine-readable JSON catalog
projects.one_liner: Find a prompt by task, fill in your own material, then copy or share it. Follow reusable workflows for multi-step work.
projects.note: Evidence labels describe research or public cases for similar tasks. The templates themselves are written for this project.

projects.title: Atlas Methods
projects.intro: The library starts with existing Skill material, preserving concrete methods, conditions and limitations before organizing it into domains. Categories, search and source filters help readers discover methods, compare sources and return to the original material.
features: Browse engineering, professional, creative and office-work domains
Search Skills and filter by topic, repository and sort order
Read public summaries and records combining multiple sources
Trace entries to fixed GitHub revisions and conversion records
projects.one_liner: Explore concrete methods drawn from real GitHub Skills, browse summaries by domain and trace them to fixed source versions.
projects.note: Organization and structural checks do not establish that every Skill has been executed. Check the original source and conditions before use.

projects.title: Communicative Acts
projects.intro: Three axes organize expression: P for purpose, O for local operations and S for style. Browse functions such as informing, requesting, negotiating and repairing relationships, then examine how the expression is organized and styled. Neighboring entries explain their differences.
features: Browse 93 purposes, 43 operations and 12 style dimensions as separate axes
Expandable axis, group and entry navigation with global search
English action words, collocations and bilingual examples for purposes and operations
Read definitions, boundary comparisons, grouping reasons and case sources
projects.one_liner: Understand what an utterance does through communicative purpose, local operations and style, with definitions, boundaries and bilingual examples.
projects.note: The counts describe the current working catalog. Constructed teaching examples are distinguished from sourced cases.

projects.title: Semantic Direction Taxonomy
projects.intro: Organized around “expression = RU + semantic direction,” this searchable reference unfolds directions into a hierarchy. Entries connect explanations with expression forms, while the sidebar supports navigation and comparison of related meanings.
features: 15 main categories, 35 subcategories and 201 semantic directions
1,058 expression forms connect directions to concrete language
Expandable tree navigation linked to the reading pane
Global search, section links and mobile reading
projects.one_liner: Explore the meanings, expression forms and English equivalents of directions such as existence, change, movement and action.

related: Lookbook's exported prompts and CSS variables exist to pin down a style when you build interfaces with AI; this guide covers building interfaces and products with AI.
The prompts can be handed to AI coding assistants such as Claude; this online book is about mastering Claude Code.
Also a browsable, searchable library for one kind of thing: design systems here, software types there.
projects.title: Lookbook
projects.sub: A visual index of design systems
projects.one_liner: Over 80 design systems from well-known products, rendered as pages you can browse, compare and take away.

feature.problem: A design system is usually just a document: colors, type, radii and components described in prose. It is hard to see what it feels like in use, and harder still to compare a few of them. Lookbook renders those specs as pages, then turns them into formats you can copy into a project.

Browse
Grouped by category, searchable in Chinese or English, filterable by dark or light.
The gallery: every card carries a brand palette and a one-line summary.
img/projects/lookbook-preview.jpg
Preview
Every template rendered as a complete sample landing page: navigation, hero, buttons, cards and footer.

Palette, type scale, radii and spacing, and every component definition. Click a color to copy it.

Compare
Put two design systems side by side on the same page, swap them, or draw two at random.

img/projects/lookbook-export.jpg
Export
AI prompts, CSS variables, Tailwind config and more, bundled in one click.
Stripe as an example: the export tab with a ready-made AI prompt.
use: Hand it to an AI coding assistant such as Claude, Cursor or v0 and have it build interfaces in the chosen style
Drop the CSS variables or Tailwind config into your own project
Import into Figma's Tokens Studio (W3C Design Tokens JSON)
Keep DESIGN.md in the project root so your coding assistant can always refer to it
tech: Each design system is one DESIGN.md; categories and summaries live in CATALOG.md, which drives the cards and filters.
One sample landing page rendered from each set of design tokens, so the systems are actually comparable.
Vite and plain JavaScript, output as a static site.
Formats are bundled into a .zip in the browser, with no backend.
Automated tests cover data parsing, every page render, export formats and text contrast; GitHub Actions deploys on push to main.

projects.intro: Each design system lives in a single DESIGN.md: colors, type, radii, spacing and components. Lookbook renders the same sample page from those tokens, so you can see what Stripe, Linear or Notion feel like without reading the spec.
features: Browse: grouped by category, searchable in Chinese or English, filterable by dark or light
Preview: every template rendered as a complete sample landing page
Inspect: palette, type scale, radii and spacing, and every component definition
Compare: put two design systems side by side, or draw two at random
Export: AI prompts, CSS variables, Tailwind config and more, bundled in one click

related: Also a local-first macOS app: no online service needed, and data stays on the machine.
Aide lets a local model call desktop tools; this guide covers giving an agent a tool system.
projects.title: Aide
projects.sub: A local AI entry point for the desktop
projects.one_liner: Call up local AI with a Mac shortcut for selected text, screenshots and desktop tasks.
projects.status: Native app in development · legacy Qt v1.4.0
projects.intro: A native SwiftUI / AppKit shell with a Python core using local Ollama models. Quick Panel handles selected text and desktop-tool requests; Workspace preserves searchable conversations. Current source adds read-aloud, Calendar operations and per-conversation opt-in web search and command-line tools. Data-changing actions show their details and wait for confirmation.
features: ⌘⌃L opens Quick Panel for selected text or desktop requests
⌘⌃S captures a region for chat; ⌘⌃R reads selected text aloud
Workspace with search, streaming Markdown, regeneration and custom agents
Notes, Reminders and Calendar operations with confirmation before changes
Per-conversation opt-in search and command-line tools, with credentials in Keychain
projects.note: The installer uses PyQt5. See the source repository for running the SwiftUI / AppKit version. Opt-in web search sends the model’s search queries to the configured provider.
projects.maintenance_note: This page describes the current native source. The public v1.4.0 installer is the older PyQt5 app; build the native app using the repository instructions. It is not notarized. Opt-in web search sends the model’s search queries to the configured provider.

related: It generates AI research reports automatically, and research reports are one starting point of the Research2Video workflow.
Research2Video turns material into a script; this project breaks the implicit thinking in writing into checkable steps.
Also a local workbench: Atlas for a library, this one for research to finished video.
projects.title: Research2Video
projects.sub: 研映 · From research to video
projects.one_liner: A local creative workspace for recurring research, scripts, video production and multi-platform publishing.
projects.intro: Matrices and columns organize audiences, sources, intended takeaways and production settings. Start with a question, research report or script, then turn the research and original material into narration, visuals, subtitles and video. An embedded assistant uses the same application capabilities as the web workspace.
features: Manage research jobs, sources and schedules by matrix and column
Write from research and original material while preserving script versions and video records
Source screenshots, focused details and data graphics synchronized with narration and subtitles
Produce full episodes or individual items and remake videos from an approved script
Publishing packages, queues and records for Bilibili, Douyin, Kuaishou and Xiaohongshu
Use the embedded assistant to query and manage sources, research, production and publishing
projects.note: The complete production environment has primarily been validated on macOS / Apple silicon. Model, speech-service and platform accounts require configuration.

related: The same idea of a browsable library, for design systems.
projects.title: Application Atlas
projects.one_liner: Find real open-source projects by software type and use case, with capabilities, conditions and source references.
projects.intro: Connect software types, application scenarios and real projects. Browse types, search projects, inspect conditions and license status, save favorites and trace sources. Research tasks retain new research and update suggestions.
features: Discover projects by software type, scenario and concrete use
Project cards state sources, license status, conditions and missing information
Search, filters, favorites and source references
Research tasks preserve progress, update suggestions and recovery paths

related: Another library that organizes one kind of thing for browsing: Application Atlas covers software types, P Atlas covers what a topic can be used to do.
The library has topics such as Codex and Claude Code; this e-book is about driving Codex to turn ideas into verifiable results.
P Atlas covers LangChain Agent, MCP and Agent Harness; this tutorial covers an agent's tool system and runtime.
projects.title: P Atlas
projects.one_liner: Explore what a topic can be used to do: every possibility states its conditions and traces back to its sources.
projects.intro: It starts from achievable outcomes rather than feature lists. Each topic has a map of possibilities: what the outcome is, which conditions and components it needs, and which sources support it, all on one card. “Source-backed” does not mean tested in practice; the page states each item's evidence status, and directions still to be verified are marked separately.
features: 38 topics across 11 domains, with topic research reports and source lists
Browse by use, filter by capability path and evidence status, or search the whole library
Each possibility lists the outcome, conditions and limits, required components and source passages
Raw entries as JSON and Markdown, plus the research validation record

projects.title: PersonalSpace
projects.sub: A native macOS personal digital space
projects.one_liner: A local-first personal library: read-only access to folders you authorize, search and preview, and reminders for what needs doing.
projects.intro: A native macOS app connecting documents, personal objects, orders, contracts, warranties and subscriptions. Authorized folders are read-only; imported files are copied into a local library. Search, preview, fact review, action reminders and backup/restore work alongside an application-wide assistant using local Ollama.
features: Count a folder before confirming indexing; track subsequent file changes
Name search, explicitly permitted full-text search and system previews
Personal objects, document links, managed copies and quick import
Review facts for orders, contracts, warranties and subscriptions; manage multiple actions and local reminders
Local Ollama assistant for finding documents, preparing matters and native operations
Sensitive-document protection, backup/restore and retained previous libraries
projects.maintenance_note: A local development and trial build. Developer ID signing, notarization and independent-account public distribution checks are not complete.

projects.title: Radar
projects.one_liner: Describe what to follow in plain language, collect on a schedule, and get events that link back to the source.
projects.intro: Describe what to follow, preview sources and collect updates on a schedule. Radar distinguishes the initial baseline from later changes, preserves original links and can merge reports of the same event. On request, local Ollama produces sourced briefings or answers questions about collected material.
features: Sources include GitHub, RSS, web pages, JSON endpoints and Hacker News
Build an initial baseline, then deduplicate and merge new events with source links
Menu-bar operation, notifications, scheduled checks and catch-up after wake
Local Ollama briefings and Q&A with traceable source references
Source coverage, missed-event analysis, source status and source export

print_books.title: Deep Dive into Data Analysis with R
print_books.sub: 深入浅出R语言数据分析
print_books.intro: Covers data analysis methods and common models, then works through case studies in R: data acquisition and web scraping, preprocessing and exploration, survival analysis, principal component analysis, linear and logistic regression, clustering, association rules, random forests, support vector machines, neural networks, text mining and social network analysis. Written for beginner and advanced R users and for data science practitioners.

print_books.title: Data Visualization with R in Practice
print_books.intro: A multi-angle guide to data visualization in R, with more than 500 worked examples covering over 30 families of statistical graphics.

print_books.title: Statistical Analysis with R in Practice
print_books.intro: Application-first coverage of commonly used R packages and the implementation of statistical methods and statistical machine learning models. Eleven chapters in four parts: R basics, statistical analysis, applications (business A/B testing, marketing analytics, credit scoring), and reproducible research with Shiny visualization.

print_books.title: Getting Started with SPSS and Data Analysis in Practice
print_books.intro: Step-by-step illustrated operations, guidance on statistical thinking, learning by doing through cases, and companion videos and materials.

ebooks.title: Mastering Codex
ebooks.sub: 驾驭 Codex · Not just using it, but steering it
ebooks.intro: Turn vague ideas into verifiable results. Understand what it does, keep your own judgment, and find your way back when it goes wrong. Eight progressive parts, 28 chapters, 7 kinds of interactive learning and 5 kinds of practical tasks.

ebooks.title: Mastering Claude
ebooks.sub: 驾驭 Claude · Not just asking, but getting it done
ebooks.intro: From first opening Claude Code Desktop to organizing complex projects, spotting wrong assumptions and verifying real deliverables. Planned as 8 parts and 32 chapters; 2 sample chapters are open now. An unofficial, independent educational project.

ebooks.title: LLM Inference Engineering in Practice
ebooks.sub: 大模型 Inference 工程实践 · From model files to a working service
ebooks.intro: Start with a small model, not a big one, and build the full range of inference engineering through experiments. Each chapter is tied to a real experiment and its run evidence. Covers prefill, decode, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, quantization, caching and concurrency.

The opening of this series: why code is not the system, and what a missing system blueprint costs.
Starting from real business processes, see how AI translates into practical workflow transformation and automation.
